artworks.title: Hector Taking Leave of Andromache
artworks.description: Oil painting by Angelica Kauffman, a founding member of the Royal Academy, now in the National Trust collection at Saltram in Devon. Hector, armed for battle, parts from the weeping Andromache and their infant son Astyanax — the farewell of the sixth book of the Iliad, where husband and wife meet for the last time before he returns to the fighting.

artworks.title: Andromache Mourning Hector
artworks.description: The history painting with which Jacques-Louis David was received into the Académie royale in 1783, now in the Louvre, Paris. Andromache grieves beside the body of Hector laid out on his bier as the child Astyanax clings to her — an echo of the laments that end the Iliad, where Andromache leads the wailing of the Trojan women over her husband.

artworks.title: Triumphant Achilles
artworks.description: Monumental fresco by the Austrian painter Franz Matsch in the main hall of the Achilleion, the palace built on Corfu for Empress Elisabeth of Austria. Achilles drives his chariot in triumph before the walls of Troy, dragging the lifeless body of Hector in the dust behind him as the Trojans watch from the ramparts.

films.title: Troy
films.description: Eric Bana's Hector is the film's moral centre — the defender who fights for a city and a family, not a goddess's vanity — until the duel with Achilles ends the Iliad's greatest warrior on a beach of sand and CGI.

films.title: Helen of Troy
films.description: Wise's widescreen epic keeps Hector as Troy's shield: the prince who holds the wall while Paris' choice unravels the house of Priam.

films.title: Troy: Fall of a City
films.description: The BBC/Netflix cycle gives Hector room to be husband, brother and captain — the farewell with Andromache staged again for a streaming age.
